★ About Winsmore

Welcome to Winsmore — a project that began when I was still at school, rating horses against each other using criteria such as going, trainer, course form, recent form, speed, and more.

The original idea was simple: compare every horse in a race across multiple categories, identify the strongest in each area, and combine those rankings into an overall score.

Over time, the system evolved into a weighted model. Each winning horse had its criteria scores added to a database, allowing the system to identify which factors were historically most important in finding winners.

For example, if races were being rated on only three criteria — going, distance, and speed — and winning horses consistently ranked highly for speed, then the speed category would receive a stronger weighting in future calculations. In other words, criteria proven to be more predictive over time were given greater importance.

In the early days this process worked well, but analysing a single race manually with the Racing Post and Sporting Life could take over an hour. Today, modern technology allows Winsmore to process far richer data, in far greater detail, and at a speed that simply was not possible before.

Winsmore still follows the same core philosophy today.

Each race is analysed using a wide range of data points, with predictions generated through the scoring and weighting of factors such as going, trainer, jockey, speed figures, Racing Post Ratings (RPR), course form, recent form, and more. Every horse is ranked against the others within each category, and those rankings are multiplied by dynamic weightings generated from historical winner data. The final combined score produces the system’s prediction, shown as the BACK bet in the “Today’s Racing” section.

Unlike many tipping services, Winsmore does not selectively choose races. Maidens, novices, hurdles, changing ground conditions, first-time blinkers and other difficult race types are all analysed equally by the system.

Despite this broad approach, the results have been consistently profitable. Since the site went live, backing every BACK selection has produced a profit of +65.7 pts in May.

That said, blindly backing every selection may not be realistic for the average punter. Winsmore is designed not only as a prediction system, but also as a detailed race analysis tool.

Using the BACK bets as a guide — alongside the detailed race cards, comparison tables, jockey and trainer statistics (overall, recent, course and horse-specific), horse profiles, and other data available on the site — users can apply their own judgement to narrow down the strongest opportunities and potentially achieve even better results.

No system can predict racing perfectly, but Winsmore aims to provide a structured, data-led approach that gives users a clearer and more informed view of every race.

★ Features — What Winsmore Does

Winsmore scores every runner in every UK race each morning with a single rating model. It names a top selection in every race — no cherry-picking — and surrounds it with the form, speed, prices and connections data you need to judge it yourself. Every pick is logged before the off and settled against Betfair Starting Price, win or lose.
📋  A rated pick in every race
The model scores and ranks every runner, then puts forward its top-rated horse in every single race — shown as the BACK bet in Today's Racing. Nothing is skipped: maidens, novices and tricky handicaps all get a prediction.
🎯  Dual Specialists (DS)
A smaller, higher-conviction angle — races where both the trainer and the jockey have a winning record at today's course. Premium-tier DS picks are flagged separately and tracked on their own.
🔢  Full rated cards & score breakdown
Every runner scored and ranked, with a small info box on each row that opens the scoring behind the number — form, speed, going, draw, official mark, trainer and jockey — so you can compare runners feature by feature.
⚡  SPD+ speed figures
Our own speed figure, built from years of UK race-time data and shown beside RP's ratings. Click it to see the horse's recent runs and the speed it clocked each time.
📈  Form, figures & comments
RPR and Top Speed on every row, plus a Form button opening recent races. Distances longer than today show red and shorter green, with today's going and course runs highlighted — alongside the Spotlight write-up and trainer comments.
🧬  Sire data (A/E)
For applicable horses we score how a sire's offspring have performed at today's distance versus expectation — above 1 is positive. Standout sires (A/E > 1.25 today) are flagged on the card.
💷  Live prices & movers
Early-morning prices sit on the cards and refresh every 15 minutes. Click any price to see the day's full movement, and a Movers panel tracks the biggest steamers and drifters.
📊  Trainer & jockey course stats
Click any trainer or jockey for their strike rate at the course, overall, and over the last 14 and 28 days, plus runners today. Single-run, high-strike-rate connections are tagged — informational, not fed into the ratings.
🔍  Insight panels
Context a bare card doesn't give you: Connections course edge, Returning Jockeys, Favourite stats, Travel Watch and draw bias.
🪄  Built for picking your own
Runner silks on every row, per-course filtering, expand/collapse all, and a [−] hide toggle next to each horse so you can clear the ones you've ruled out and leave just your shortlist.
✅  A results record you can check
The Performance section shows every system's record — strike rate, points profit/loss and ROI — with separate Back and DS histories and a monthly chart, all settled at Betfair SP. Each day's page stays published in the archive, so you can verify any claim against what we put up before racing.

How the ratings work

1
Overnight results come in. Yesterday's races are settled at Betfair SP and every horse's form profile is rebuilt from years of UK racing data.
2
Every runner is scored. The model weighs ability ratings, speed figures, form trajectory, course / distance / going suitability, the handicap mark, draw bias and trainer & jockey records — tuned separately for handicaps and conditions races.
3
A pick is named in every race. The top-rated horse is put forward in each race, with the Dual Specialist angle layered on top where the connections qualify.
4
Everything is logged. Each pick goes into the record before racing starts and is settled at Betfair SP after — that's the performance data you see on the site.

★ How to Bet on Betfair Exchange & Get Better Odds

The Betfair Exchange lets you take the Betfair Starting Price (BSP) — the true market price at race-off. This is ALWAYS better than the bookies by 10–50% in our experience. Here’s exactly how to do it.

1
Join Betfair
Go to betfair.com/exchange/plus and create a free account if you haven’t already.
2
Use the Exchange — NOT the Sportsbook
Once logged in, click Exchange at the top of the page — not Sportsbook. The Exchange is where BSP and real market prices live. The Sportsbook is just a regular bookmaker.
📝 Look for the two tabs: ExchangeSportsbook — always choose Exchange.
3
Find the Race & Choose Your Market
Navigate to today’s race. At the top of the market you’ll see several tabs — you need to pick the right one before clicking your horse:
Win — Your horse must win the race. Best liquidity, easiest to get BSP matched.
Top 2 / Top 3 / Top 4 Finishers — Place-only bets. Choose the tab that matches how many places the race pays. As a guide: 5–7 runners = 2 places, 8–15 runners = 3 places, 16+ runners = 4 places. Same odds 1000 / stake £1 / Take SP process as the Win bet — just a separate bet slip.
⚠️ Each Way tab — combines win + place in one bet but has very low liquidity on the Exchange. It’s harder to get BSP matched cleanly. We recommend doing two separate bets instead: one in the Win market and one in the Top 2/3/4 market. Same result, much better liquidity on both.
4
Click the Blue Cell Next to Your Horse
Once you’re in the right market tab, find your horse in the grid and click the blue cell next to its odds — this opens a bet slip on the right.
🔵 The blue cells are the Back prices (bet the horse to finish as selected). The pink cells are the Lay prices — ignore those.
5
Set Odds to 1000 & Stake to £1
In the bet slip you’ll see two boxes: Odds and Stake.
⚠️ Be careful! Set Odds = 1000 and Stake = £1. Do not mix them up — you do NOT want £1000 stake at odds of 1!
Your bet will show: Liability: £1.00 — you only ever risk £1.
6
Click “Place Bets”
Hit the yellow Place Bets button. Because 1000/1 won’t be matched by the market, it will appear under Unmatched Bets — this is exactly what we want. If betting Win + Place separately, repeat steps 3–6 for the place market now.
7
Select “Take SP” and click Update
In the Receipt / Unmatched Bets panel, select Take SP from the three radio options (Cancel / Keep / Take SP), then click the yellow Update button. Do this for each unmatched bet.
✅ Done! Your bet will be matched at Betfair Starting Price at race-off — automatically, with no further action needed.

💡 Why does this work?

By requesting 1000/1 the bet is never matched before the race. Selecting Take SP tells Betfair to match it at the Betfair Starting Price when the race goes off — a price calculated from real money in the market. BSP is ALWAYS better than the bookmakers, typically 10–50% better odds. Your liability is just £1, so there’s no risk of an accidental large bet. For Win + Place together, total liability is just £2. Our data shows this approach beats E/W on the Exchange for liquidity every time.

StepActionKey Detail
1Join Betfairbetfair.com/exchange/plus
2Choose ExchangeNOT Sportsbook
3Choose Market tabWin  |  Top 2/3/4 (place)  |  avoid Each Way tab (low liquidity)
4Click blue cellOpens bet slip for that horse
5Set odds & stakeOdds = 1000  |  Stake = £1
6Place BetsShows as Unmatched — repeat for place market if doing Win+Place
7Take SP → UpdateBSP at race-off — 10–50% better than bookies

★ Race FAQ — How to Read the Race Card

Every runner row is packed with information — ratings, stats, form figures and tags. This guide explains what each piece means, section by section.

Runner header line

Silks
The jockey's racing colours (jacket/cap), shown as a small icon next to the saddle number.
Name & odds
Horse name followed by the current best-priced odds (e.g. 55/1), shown as a fraction.
Runs/Wins
Career totals in the form 15r/4w — 15 runs, 4 wins.

Stats & rating pills

Trainer/Jockey badge
e.g. Carson: 4W/10R (40%) — that connection's win rate at this course (wins / rides, win %). Shown when a trainer or jockey has a notable record here.
T: / J:
The horse's trainer and jockey for today's race.
OR
Official Rating — the BHA's handicap mark for the horse. Higher = rated better.
FRM
Form rating — a raw speed/form figure from the horse's recent runs, shown as a dot scale (more filled dots = stronger recent figures).
SPD
Speed — recent-form speed figure, also shown as a dot scale.
SPD+
Our own in-house speed figure, built from actual race times against course/distance/going par times (centred on 100). Shown alongside FRM/SPD for comparison — it does not affect the model's picks, it's purely an extra data point we're tracking.
Form
Recent finishing positions (most recent first) plus how long ago the last run was, e.g. Form: 113-29 50d ago. A dash (-) separates seasons; 0 = finished outside the top 9.
SireAE
The sire's Actual-vs-Expected strike rate — how often that sire's progeny win relative to what the market price would predict. Above 1.00 = outperforming, below 1.00 = underperforming.
Spotlight
Racing Post's pre-race verdict/analysis on the horse — tap to read the full text.
Comment icon
Opens RP's most recent run-by-run comments for the horse.

Feature delta pills

These small +/- pills (e.g. SPD -1.49, DRAW +0.64, GOING -0.59, DIST -0.58) show how this horse compares to the race average on each individual factor the model scores. Green = above the field average on that factor (helps the horse), red = below average (hurts it). The pills shown are whichever factors most influenced the horse's overall score — common ones include:

FRM / SPD / SPD+
Speed figure comparisons.
COURSE / DIST / GOING
Course form, distance form and ground (going) preference.
DRAW
Stall/draw position bias for this course and distance.
TRAINER / JOCKEY
Connections' course strike-rate edge.
OR
Official Rating compared to the field.

Tags & labels

NAP / NB / TIP
Tooleys Tips — our top 3 selections of the day, ranked by confidence (NAP = strongest, NB = next best, TIP = third pick).
Dual Specialist (DS)
A horse whose trainer and jockey both have a winning record at this course. The 'Sole Booking' tag highlights when this exact trainer/jockey pairing has teamed up here before.
Value Bet
A horse the model rates as a bigger overlay (better price) than the market suggests — calculated from our win-probability model vs. the morning odds. Shown with an 'edge %'.
Confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
How clear-cut the model's top selection is in that race — based on the scoring gap between the top horse and its closest rival.
★ (star)
Marks the model's single back-pick selection for that race.
⚠ MARKET DISAGREES
Warning shown when our top-rated horse is a big-priced outsider (20/1+) — the market sees it very differently to the model, so treat with extra caution.
First time on this horse
This jockey has never ridden this particular horse before — an unknown combination.
NR
Non-runner — the horse was declared but withdrawn before the race; any bet is void (stake returned, no win/loss).

Tip

Tap any rating, badge or tag on a runner row to open a detailed pop-up with the full breakdown and history behind it.

📱 WinSmore App

Installing is completely optional — the website works exactly the same in your browser. If you'd like, you can add WinSmore to your device for a faster, full-screen experience with its own home-screen icon.

Notifications are separate: use the 🔔 bell button at the bottom-left of the screen to turn standout-bet alerts on or off — you don't need to install the app for those.

📝 Dashboard Updates & New Features

◆
Added Trainer and Jockey stats click name, runners for the day, strike rate at course/overall/14 & 28 days.
◆
Trainers and Jockeys that have only 1 run at the course and have a high strike rate tagged. Note these are informational and not included in predictions at present.
◆
Added a [-] next to horse name in the race card for hiding that horse from the card, good for picking own horses and removing the non chosen.
◆
SPD+ - own speed figures clickable on race card showing recent races and speeds
◆
Horse silks now shown on race card
◆
Prices updated every 15 mins, odds clickable on race card, pop up daily price movements
◆
New best Value Bets(At time of generation), 5 per day in the Value Bets tab, and in Todays Racing tab highlighted red. Horses in the top 3 ranks with odds greater than 8/1
◆
Form stats and comments have been added for each horse, additionally a Form button for predictions shown on the dashboard.
◆
Form will show races that were longer than todays distance in red, less in green.
◆
Spotlight data added.
◆
Most areas now clickable bringing up further data and history.
◆
The previous runs text on the race-card (27r/9w) shows all previous runs on going and distance, todays distance and going shown to compare. Runs at this course shown in addition.
◆
Small info box on race-card next to odds and horse name brings up scoring system per criteria, easily compare to other runners visually.
◆
Sire data added, shows a score for applicable horses how the offspring of sire have performed at todays distance compared to the expected. 1 < positive.
◆
Prices now updated every 15 mins from 7.30am
◆
Clicking on odds on race card shows the days price movements, new Mover tab shows top steamers and drifters since morning prices.
◆
New App mode - Click install will turn Winsmore into an app - locate app on homepage (W)
◆
New notification - Bottom left of screen a bell allows you to turn notifications on/off - At present these will just be the horses with best model pick + DS specialist 6.0+ - likely on average 1 per day, at present this running overall at 45% SR +40% ROI - last month 61% SR 120% ROI
